newsitem.title: UK: DLR EDGING UP IN EUROPE BUT STAYS IN DAY'S RANGE.
newsitem.headline: DLR EDGING UP IN EUROPE BUT STAYS IN DAY'S RANGE.

text.p: LONDON, Aug 12 Reuter) - The dollar edged up from earlier lows against the mark and yen by Europe's midsession but was still keeping well within session ranges in quiet trade.

The Bundesbank's decision to keep its repo rate steady at a fixed 3.0 percent at its tender on Tuesday initially gave the dollar a lift, but the prospect of tighter money-market rates in forthcoming repo tenders put the brakes on further dollar gains, said dealers.
"The Bundesbank is keeping the market guessing, but the market is also wary of being too long dollars after Friday's sell-off," said a UK bank dealer.

By 1120 GMT, dollar/mark was trading at 1.8625/30, up from a session low of around 1.8550 but still below the post-Bubundesbank repo news high just above 1.87 marks. It stood at 1.8545/55 late Monday in Europe.

Speculation of higher German rates remained alive because Germany's central bank only announced one fortnightly tender this week, putting the focus on what the Bundesbank will do at next week's tender.
Dealers said this uncertainty is likely to keep dollar/mark off its recent highs for now, but solid U.S. fundamentals are seen providing good support.

By 1120 GMT, dollar/mark was trading at 1.8625/30, up from a session low of around 1.8550 but still below the post-Buba repo news high just above 1.87 marks. It stood at 1.8545/55 late Monday in Europe.

Speculation about higher German rates has been kept alive as the German central bank only announced one fortnightly tender this week, putting the focus on what the Bundesbank will do at next week's tender.
Dealers said this uncertainty is likely to keep dollar/mark off its recent highs for now but solid U.S. fundamentals are also seen providing good support.

"The tone is one of consolidation, the dollar was looking overbought and there is no fresh news to buy the dollar," said Claudio Demolli, currency strategist at Merrill Lynch in London. "But it's still well supported by fundamental factors."
With no major U.S. data due today, dealers said the market was focused on Wednesday's retail sales and producer price data for July and Thursday's July consumer price numbers.

Growing concerns of inflationary pressures creeping into the U.S. economy knocked U.S. assets lower last week which also pressured the dollar, but these factors are expected to provide dollar support longer term, said analysts.
Dollar/yen, meantime, was also edging higher at the European midsession, trading back above 116 yen but still lacked the legs to take it above Monday's high around 116.35 yen.
Dealers said the market was reluctant to build up long dollar positions against the yen after Friday's four-yen decline and seemed content with consolidating around this 116 level.
"People are quite happy to stay on the sidelines of dollar/yen, it looks like we're entering a pretty quiet period for the dollar/yen," said the UK bank dealer.
Dollar/yen stood at 116.00/05 from 115.75/80 late Monday.
